Root cause confirmed empirically by grepping the shipped claude binary (it's
a de-minified JS bundle, readable via grep -a): the /model picker's menu-row
builder is `{value:"opus", label: process.env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_NAME
?? <raw id>, ...}` (same pattern for sonnet/haiku/fable). tier-set was only
writing the bare _MODEL var, so the picker silently mislabeled every row with
whatever the tier system had bound there.

Fix: tier-set.sh and tier-reconcile.sh now also write the companion
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL_NAME vars (canonical display name
per tier-derive --name <id>, e.g. "Fable 5", "Opus 4.8") alongside the _MODEL
vars, so the picker always shows the model a row actually is. This is a
labeling fix, not an architecture change -- the alias-remapping mechanism
(agents route through the opus/sonnet/haiku aliases) is unchanged.
